title: Roadmap & Launch Readiness: June Release - Engineering Sync
topics: QA signoff criteria and blocking bugs
summary: Internal roadmap/launch readiness sync for the June release. Team reviewed the recent incident regression affecting p99 latency on Dedicated pools, decided on mitigations (kernel change rollback + config tweaks), clarified outstanding QA blockers, and finalized canary rollout windows. Action items assigned for infra fixes, telemetry dashboards, and an updated runbook. Next step is a focused engineering slot for the rollback and a re-check on 2026-04-04.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-28
Time: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Avery Kim, Diego Ramos, Priya Patel, Marcus Lee, Ellen Cho, Samir Gupta, Nina Zhou

Summary: quick check-in on June release readiness; address last week's performance incident and align on rollout steps.

Topics: Launch checklist, incident postmortem, performance telemetry, canary plan, QA blockers.

[00:00] Avery Kim: Alright, good morning team, thanks for joining. I want to kick off with the incident recap from last Tuesday and then move into the launch checklist. We have about an hour.
[00:20] Diego Ramos: Yup, I'll start with the incident — so on 2026-03-20 we saw a p99 spike on Dedicated clusters after the kernel patch that rolled earlier that day. It showed up as tail latency increase around the 500ms to 900ms range for some longer sequences.
[00:38] Priya Patel: Yeah, SRE saw increased queuing at the serving layer, plus KV cache miss amplification. We suspected the kernel change made some preemption behavior worse, and autoscaler kept packing pods which exacerbated work-stealing.
[01:05] Marcus Lee: To be clear, it wasn't the model weights or quant; model inference time was stable at the kernel call level, but the host scheduling and context switches seemed to add jitter.
[01:20] Ellen Cho: Right, infra telemetry showed CPU steal time uptick and I/O syscall latency rose. Some of our kernels have different syscall patterns with the new kernel. I think a rollback to previous kernel build reduces the p99 immediately in staging.
[01:38] Avery Kim: Okay so we have a candidate mitigation: rollback kernel on Dedicated. What's the risk surface there? Are we trading off something else?
[01:55] Diego Ramos: There is a minor security backport missing on the older kernel, but it's within our control — we can apply the security patch and still use older kernel base. The immediate priority is to stabilize tail latency for launch.
[02:10] Priya Patel: Also autoscaler thresholds need a tweak. The default bin-packing policy is grouping small workloads together to save cost, but at high concurrency that increases context switches. We should temporarily loosen the packing to reserve headroom.
[02:30] Samir Gupta: From QA perspective, the regression manifests in long-running chat sessions where the KV cache lookup pattern is more intense. QA ran the smoke suite and there were intermittent 5xx errors during the spike window.
[02:50] Nina Zhou: Telemetry note: our dashboards didn't show the p99 uptick quickly enough because we didn't have aggregation on KV cache hit rate per route. I'll add a metric to track p99 for KV-hit vs KV-miss.
[03:05] Avery Kim: Good. So immediate actions are kernel rollback + autoscaler tweak + KV cache telemetry. Diego, Priya, Marcus — who owns which?
[03:18] Diego Ramos: I'll drive the rollback, coordinate with Ellen to stage infra changes.
[03:22] Priya Patel: I'll adjust autoscaler thresholds and watch for saturation, and set an alert for queue length.
[03:26] Marcus Lee: I'll add the KV cache p99 metric and update the dashboard, and will add an alert for p99 crossing 700ms.
[03:40] Avery Kim: Samir, can QA produce a repro run for staging after the rollback?
[03:44] Samir Gupta: Yes, I can queue a regression run once Diego deploys the rollback. I need two business days for full coverage but can do a focused run overnight.
[03:52] Avery Kim: Great. Next, checklist for June release — where are we on documentation, compliance, and runbook?
[04:05] Ellen Cho: Runbook draft exists, but needs canary steps filled in. Right now it's high level: deploy to canary region, run warmup traffic, monitor p50/p95/p99, then expand. We need explicit rollback steps and contact list.
[04:22] Diego Ramos: Also need to lock down the model pin for launch. We're currently testing ModelX-v3 but there is a last-minute change that could shift tokenization slightly. Product asked for QA to validate output regressions.
[04:36] Avery Kim: Let's not change the model at the last minute. If ModelX-v3 introduces any drift, we postpone that model version until after launch. We need deterministic outputs for customers.
[04:50] Marcus Lee: Agreed. On caching and batching, I want to suggest a small quantization profile change that saves ~8% CPU, but I need to validate it doesn't increase variance on longer contexts. It's lower risk but should be part of canary tests.
[05:10] Priya Patel: Side note: the Dedicated pools for enterprise customers need audit log retention settings validated. Compliance asked for 90-day retention plus kms key rotation notes. Ellen, do you have that?
[05:22] Ellen Cho: Yes, infra will provide the retention policy and KMS integration doc. I'll attach it to the runbook.
[05:30] Avery Kim: Perfect. Let's move through blockers: Samir, any QA blockers left that would prevent rollout?
[05:38] Samir Gupta: Blocking issues right now: the p99 regression (we've covered that), two flaky E2E tests around conversational context reset, and one alerting gap — we don't have a per-route error budget alert.
[05:52] Nina Zhou: I can wire up per-route error budget alerts; we have the traces, just need to define thresholds. Suggest 0.5% error budget per route for launch.
[06:05] Avery Kim: OK set 0.5% as a starting point. We'll iterate.
[06:12] [~pause, chatter about calendar invites and docs link]
[06:40] Diego Ramos: Quick note on rollout windows — we should schedule canary during low traffic window for EU region, target 0200-0500 UTC so we have quiet traffic and the ability to rollback without too many impacted sessions.
[06:55] Priya Patel: We also need to reserve capacity in case of rollback — set aside 20% buffer so autoscaler can't immediately reclaim nodes. Ellen, can infra reserve that?
[07:07] Ellen Cho: Yes, we can set capacity reservation flags for canary. We'll do two-region canary: eu-west and us-west with reserve nodes.
[07:18] Avery Kim: Who will be primary on-call for the canary? Priya?
[07:22] Priya Patel: I can be primary, Diego secondary. We'll document escalation.
[07:30] Marcus Lee: One other technical detail: the KV cache compaction we introduced last month has a tuning parameter that might interact with rollback. If we rollback kernel but leave compaction aggressive, it could mask improvements. I'd like to temporarily reduce compaction frequency during the canary.
[07:48] Diego Ramos: Sounds reasonable. Marcus, can you create a toggle flag for compaction frequency and set default for canary?
[07:54] Marcus Lee: Yep, I'll add a feature flag and a quick toggle in config.
[08:00] Samir Gupta: On the QA timeline — if rollback goes on 2026-03-30 then I can run the overnight focused regression and have preliminary results by 2026-03-31 morning. Full regression report by 2026-04-01.
[08:15] Avery Kim: Good. Let's capture explicit dates. We'll plan rollback on 2026-03-30 03:00 UTC, focused QA overnight, and a follow-up sync 2026-04-04 to greenlight rollout.
[08:26] Priya Patel: Also, the autoscaler adjustment I'll make deploys as a hotfix and should be safe to revert. I'll also add a temporary alert when node packing exceeds 85%.
[08:38] Nina Zhou: Dashboard updates: I'll add KV cache p99, per-route p99, and per-route error budget alerts. Also add a short-latency histogram so we can distinguish queuing vs inference time.
[08:55] Avery Kim: Any risks we haven't covered? Security/compliance?
[09:00] Ellen Cho: The only outstanding compliance check was the KMS rotation note; otherwise SOC2 artifacts are in place for the release. We need to confirm retention settings with legal — I'll ping Legal and attach the confirmation doc.
[09:14] Diego Ramos: On the rollback steps, I'll prepare a playbook: commands, expected state, how to validate, and rollback-if-not-improved. I'll share before the focused engineering window.
[09:25] Samir Gupta: QA will validate canary with a small synthetic suite and some sampled production-like traces. We'll coordinate test data with Nina to ensure coverage.
[09:35] Avery Kim: OK let's recap — action owners and due dates (see runbook). We'll also update the Confluence page and notify the support rotation.
[09:45] [Cross-talk as people confirm they will do items]
[10:00] Avery Kim: Final note: do not introduce model version changes during rollback; pin model to the current validated variant. If anyone absolutely needs a model change, escalate to product and delay rollout.
[10:15] Diego Ramos: Understood.
[10:20] Avery Kim: Alright thanks everyone. We'll close and follow up via the runbook and a short stand-up on 2026-03-30.
[10:30] Meeting end.

Notes about transcription: some terms may be mis-transcribed (e.g., K-V cash, VP C), and speaker labels are approximate. The transcript is intentionally left as a raw conversational export. Links shared during the call: https://confluence.redwood/roadmap/june-launch (runbook draft), https://dashboards.redwood/telemetry/kv-cache (KV metrics - internal), runbook attachment: "canary-rollout-v1.docx".
